requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.

Where the rear lamp ESA is (part of) a light source, the approval number according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128 granted to this ESA shall be specified, or a Technical Service test report shall show that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every rear lamp ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
The rear lamp ESA shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for radiated emissions.
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The measured broadband emission values of the rear lamp ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The narrowband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA, measured by the method described in Annex 8, shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

The narrowband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA, measured by the method described in Annex 8, shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
The narrowband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA, measured by the method described in Annex 8, shall be constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The measured narrowband emission value of the rear lamp ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines by the rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
Where tested by the stripline method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the TEM cell method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the BCI method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the ALSE method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the ALSE method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the reverberation chamber method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the reverberation chamber method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the stripline method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the TEM cell method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the BCI method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the ALSE method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the ALSE method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
Where tested by the reverberation chamber method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
The rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of the rear lamp ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

Where the rear lamp ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, it shall be tested with the starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V systems) with 10 pulses, classified according to the functional status classification defined in ISO 16750-1.

For the starting profile, rear lamp ESA functions related to immunity related functions shall meet functional status B where the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, and functional status C otherwise.
For the starting profile, rear lamp ESA functions not related to immunity related functions shall meet functional status D.
For test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) with 500 pulses, the rear lamp ESA shall meet FPSC III for functions related and not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) with 500 pulses, the rear lamp ESA shall meet FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) with 10 pulses, the rear lamp ESA shall meet FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, the rear lamp ESA shall meet FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, the rear lamp ESA shall meet FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The rear lamp ESA shall meet the immunity requirements throughout the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
The rear lamp electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall limit conducted transients emitted from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

Each lamp that is part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated rear lamp unit (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) shall satisfy the provisions of UN Regulation No. 148 or of another applicable Regulation.
Every rear lamp belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the rear lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The value for "a" in the size of the approval marking on the rear lamp shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking of the rear lamp shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark on the rear lamp.
Where the rear position lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.

Where the reversing lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately and has a reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The rear lamp shall bear the approval marking.
The rear lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Where the rear lamp has an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control, a secondary operating mode and/or non-replaceable light sources, the rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used in the rear lamp, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used in the rear lamp, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
The specific identification code of the light source module shall comprise the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle.
Where several non-identical light source modules are used, the approval mark on the light source module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
The approval mark on the light source module and the approval mark on the lamp in which the module is used shall be from the same applicant.
The light source module shall be marked with the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
The lamp shall be marked with the specific identification code of the light source module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a) shall be affixed on the light source module component.

The size of the components of a single approval mark on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The lamp shall meet the requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 148.
The stop lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
The reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, the lamp shall either comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, without exceeding the maximum intensities when all light sources are illuminated, or produce a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
The rear lamp shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall meet its photometric and colorimetric requirements with a voltage supplied at the lamp of 13.5 V for 12 Volt-Systems.

Where the lamp is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and uses light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall meet its requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the lamp shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the lamp shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the lamp shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or not less than the intensity value specified in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the lamp shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The luminous intensities of the lamp shall comply with the requirements when tested according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted by the lamp shall comply with the colorimetric requirements inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, when tested according to the procedure of paragraph 4.8.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted by the lamp shall be observed.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 4.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 10.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The rear lamp shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under UN R148.

The luminous intensity of each light function of the rear lamp shall, for the various directions of measurement, be at least the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Figures A3-I to A3-XV, unless specified otherwise, with the direction H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference.

Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity of each light function of the rear lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

For the reversing lamp, where visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
The light emitted by each light function of mass-produced rear lamps shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148.
The mechanical and geometric characteristics of the mass-produced rear lamp shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations.

For a mass-produced rear lamp chosen at random and tested for the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
The lamp shall withstand a one-hour test of continuous operation following a warm-up period of 20 minutes at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C.
After the heat resistance test and stabilization at the ambient temperature, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification of the lamp shall be perceptible.

In case of doubt after the heat resistance test, the luminous intensity of the lamp measured according to paragraph 5. of UN R148 shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.

For a reversing lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For a reversing lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For the rear position lamp and stop lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For the rear position lamp and stop lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
The retro-reflector shall be marked with the approval number assigned to its type, following the requirements of paragraph 3.3. of UN R150.

Every retro-reflector belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking of the retro-reflector shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number of the retro-reflector approval marking shall be placed close to the approval mark.
Where the approval marking of the retro-reflector is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the prescribed format.
The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflector shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.

Where the retro-reflector is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with lamps and a single approval mark is used, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
The retro-reflector shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN Regulation No. 150.
The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
The retro-reflector shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
The components of the retro-reflector or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough.
Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflector, when illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.), shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
The retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
The retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

The retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective device.
The retro-reflector shall meet the general specifications of paragraph 4. and the specifications of shape and dimensions of Annex 5.

The retro-reflector, after the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6, shall meet the colorimetric characteristics of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
The retro-reflector shall withstand the water penetration test of Part 2 of Annex 6 and subsequently the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants of Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7.

The retro-reflector shall, if necessary, withstand the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 and subsequently the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device of Part 5 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector shall meet the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective devices of Part 3 of Annex 4.
The retro-reflector shall withstand the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6.

The retro-reflector, after undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., shall have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

Where more than one or a range of different axes of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the red retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements for each specified axis of reference or for the extreme axes of reference of the specified range.

For Class IA or IB red retro-reflectors, when measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the red retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

For a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP", the RI at the position of minimum RI, obtained by rotation about its axis of reference with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5 of this Regulation) and an angle of divergence of 20', shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5 of this Regulation.

For a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP", the RI measured at the other angles of illumination and divergence, with the device in the position corresponding to the minimum-RI value of ε, shall attain the specified values, with the device allowed to be rotated about its axis of reference by ±5° from that position if the specified values are not attained.

For a retro-reflective device marked "TOP", the RI shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during rotation about its axis by ±5°, with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 4 of this Regulation) and an angle of divergence of 20'.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.
No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit of the retro-reflector after the water penetration test.

Upon completion of the drain period after the water spray test, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the retro-reflector device, nor shall one be able to be formed by tapping or tilting the device.

The retro-reflector shall resist dust penetration when exposed to test dust agitated at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, with the dust allowed to settle between the agitation periods.
The retro-reflector shall be so designed that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.
The front surface of the retro-reflector shall resist tarnishing, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.
The protection of the rear face of the retro-reflector shall resist deterioration, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The rear lamp combined with the retro-reflector, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
The retro-reflector sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device immediately after completion of the corrosion test.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after the corrosion test and a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9.
The retro-reflector shall withstand exposure in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013, using the parameters given in Table A6-1, for a period of 500 hours.

The outer surface of the retro-reflector, and in particular its illuminating surface, shall not show any apparent surface changes, other than slight surface cracks, when inspected visually about five minutes after being lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol.

Where the retro-reflector is a moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB, its RI shall meet the requirements of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of UN R150 when measured after its outer surface, and in particular its illuminating surface, has been lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil and cleaned after about 5 minutes.
The approval number on the retro-reflector shall be placed close to the circle surrounding the letter "E", in any position in relation to it.
The digits constituting the approval number on the retro-reflector shall face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflector shall be placed diametrically opposite the approval number.

The rear lamp shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
It shall not be possible for the rear lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.

The reference axis of the rear lamp light-signalling functions and retro-reflector, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

The reference axis of the rear lamp light-signalling functions and retro-reflector, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
The rear lamp shall be fitted in compliance with any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer.
In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except for a matched pair of a function.

The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each function of the rear lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red lamps of the rear lamp (rear position lamp and stop lamp) if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front by each red lamp of the rear lamp, as verified during type approval of the lamps, shall be not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be such that it can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps if they exist, the side-marker lamps if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp.
The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall not be concealed.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be red.
The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.

Where the rear lamp has been tested, according to its type approval documentation, by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the rear lamp shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of each lamp of the rear lamp observed from infinity, except for obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the rear lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

Each lamp (device) of the rear lamp shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in paragraph 6 of UN Regulation No. 48 when installed on a vehicle.
The reversing lamp shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
The number of S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be two.
The stop lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 category vehicles, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of an S1 or S2 category stop lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be positioned not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.

The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except for optional rear position lamps.
The rear position lamp shall be installed at a height above the ground of not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm.

To be considered visible, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
The rear position lamp shall have a closed-circuit tell-tale, except when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The closed-circuit tell-tale of the rear position lamp shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
The point on the illuminating surface of the reversing lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON, except that they may be switched OFF and remain switched OFF as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).

The position of each lamp in width, in height and in length shall be such that the measured distances fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, in accordance with the general requirements of paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of UN Regulation No. 48.

The angles of geometric visibility of each lamp of the rear lamp, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The rear lamp shall not emit white light visible towards the rear, except as permitted in paragraph 5.10. (reversing lamp), when checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10.
The red light of the rear lamp shall not be visible towards the front, when checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10.
Every lamp of the rear lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle shall function when switched on.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the lamps of the rear lamp, verified by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall fulfil the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. and in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
